name: 2WD robot car chassis
description: Mechanical part: the acrylic base of a 2-wheel-drive robot with two TT motors, 65 mm wheels and a front caster. It has no pins. Put it in a project with a "world" block and two dc-motor parts: the physics engine drives it with the motors' speeds and moves the robot around the arena.

props.label: Wheel radius
props.description: Drive wheel radius (65 mm TT wheels → 3.25 cm).

props.label: Track width
props.description: Distance between the two drive wheels' contact points.

props.label: Length
props.description: Body length (front to back), used for collisions.

props.label: Width
props.description: Body width (including the wheels), used for collisions.

props.label: Mass
props.description: Total mass with motors, boards and batteries.

props.label: Tyre grip
props.description: Friction coefficient between the tyres and the floor (rubber on wood ≈ 0.8, on tiles ≈ 0.5).

props.label: Sensor offset
props.description: How far in front of the wheel axle the forward sensor (HC-SR04) sits. The axle is a quarter of the length behind the body centre, so 15 cm puts it at the front edge of a 20 cm body.

bindings.description: Robot body centre x in the world (cm), written by the physics engine.
Robot body centre y (cm); y grows downwards like the canvas.
How many times the robot hit a wall or obstacle since reset.
Smallest gap to any wall/obstacle so far (cm); 9999 before the world starts.
Gap to the nearest wall/obstacle now (cm).
Echo of the wheelRadius prop (cm), read by the physics engine.
